---
title: "{{< fa brands github >}} Step 5: Connect GitHub"
---

[Due by **{{< var due.setup >}}**]{.highlight-yellow}

On the day, the {{< gl agent >}} opens {{< gl issue display="issues" >}} and {{< gl "pull request" display="pull requests" >}} on your {{< gl repository >}} for you. For that it needs to talk to GitHub from the {{< gl terminal >}}, which the {{< gl "GitHub CLI" >}} provides. Two parts: install the GitHub CLI and log in, then create a `dev` {{< gl branch >}}.

## {{< fa key >}} Part 1: The GitHub CLI

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS

The {{< gl "GitHub CLI" >}} comes through {{< gl Homebrew >}}, the package manager for the Mac. If you do not have Homebrew yet, go to [brew.sh](https://brew.sh/), copy the install line shown at the top of that page, paste it into {{< gl terminal display="Terminal" >}}, press Enter, and follow the prompts. It asks for your Mac password and takes a few minutes. Then, in the same Terminal window, install the GitHub CLI:

```bash
brew install gh
```

### Windows

Open {{< gl PowerShell >}} (as in step 4), paste this line, and press Enter:

```powershell
winget install --id GitHub.cli --source winget
```

Close the {{< gl terminal >}} and open a new window afterwards, so the new program is found.

:::

Now connect the CLI to your GitHub account. In the terminal, run:

```bash
gh auth login
```

It asks a few questions. Answer **GitHub.com**, **HTTPS**, **Yes** to authenticating Git with your GitHub {{< gl credential display="credentials" >}}, and **Login with a web browser**. Copy the one-time code it shows, press Enter, paste the code into the browser page that opens, and authorize.

Check it worked:

```bash
gh auth status
```

Then open a terminal at your setup {{< gl repository >}} (as in step 4) and run one command that only works when GitHub is reachable:

```bash
gh repo view
```

It prints the name and {{< gl README >}} of `setup-USERNAME`.

::: {.callout-note}
## The token from the first workshop

The {{< gl "personal access token" >}} you created for the first workshop keeps working for RStudio. The {{< gl "GitHub CLI" >}} has its own login, which is what you just did. The two do not interfere.
:::

## {{< fa code-branch >}} Part 2: A `dev` branch

The working pattern for the day is that changes land on a {{< gl branch >}} called `dev`, get reviewed in a {{< gl "pull request" >}}, and reach `main` through the {{< gl merge >}}. Create the branch now so it is there when the {{< gl agent >}} starts working.

Create it on your own {{< gl repository >}} from step 1, the one with your data, which is where the day's work happens. Open that project in RStudio with **File, Open Project**.

In the {{< gl "Git pane" >}}, click the **New Branch** button. Name it `dev`, leave **Sync branch with remote** ticked, and click **Create**. RStudio creates the branch, switches to it, and pushes it to GitHub.

Check on GitHub: the branch menu on your repository page now lists `main` and `dev`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Not using RStudio

Create a {{< gl branch >}} called `dev` and {{< gl push >}} it with whatever tool you prefer. The name is what matters.
:::
